summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and microscopic colitis, was readmitted one week after prior discharge due to recurrent nausea, vomiting, and persistent watery diarrhea. She had recently increased her Florinef dose without symptom relief and developed an adrenal crisis, likely exacerbated by malabsorption from chronic diarrhea. In the ED, she received IV hydrocortisone and was stabilized. Labs showed hyponatremia and hyperkalemia, consistent with adrenal insufficiency. She improved with IV fluids and stress-dose steroids, with resolution of nausea and vomiting. Abdominal ultrasound was normal, and stool studies were negative for infection. She remained on home medications including prednisone, Florinef, levothyroxine, and metoprolol. The chronic diarrhea was attributed to microscopic colitis, and outpatient GI follow-up was arranged. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue current medications, maintain a high-salt diet, and seek care if symptoms recurred.
